questions.subtopic: Exact mass: select a molecular formula
questions.prompt: An electron-impact mass spectrum has an intact molecular-ion peak at m/z 46.0419. The only possible formulae are C₂H₆O and CH₂O₂. Precise atomic masses: ¹²C = 12.000000, ¹H = 1.007825, ¹⁶O = 15.994915. Show the exact mass of each candidate, identify the consistent molecular formula and explain why a nominal mass of 46 alone is insufficient to identify it.
markPoints: C₂H₆O has exact neutral atomic mass 2(12.000000) + 6(1.007825) + 15.994915.
Calculated mass of C₂H₆O is 46.041865 u (approximately 46.0419).
CH₂O₂ has exact neutral atomic mass 12.000000 + 2(1.007825) + 2(15.994915).
Calculated mass of CH₂O₂ is 46.005480 u (approximately 46.0055).
The observed precise peak is consistent with C₂H₆O, not CH₂O₂.
Both candidates have nominal mass 46; precise mass distinguishes formulae but does not uniquely establish a structural isomer.

questions.prompt: On paper, draw the two different stereoisomers of but-2-ene, CH₃CH=CHCH₃, with every group around the C=C shown. Label E and Z, explain the priority comparison, and explain why the two drawings cannot readily interconvert by rotation about the double bond.
markPoints: Both structures retain the same CH₃–CH=CH–CH₃ atom connectivity.
Each alkene carbon is bonded to two different groups, CH₃ and H.
On each double-bond carbon CH₃ has higher CIP priority than H.
E-but-2-ene is drawn with the two methyl groups on opposite sides of the C=C.
Z-but-2-ene is drawn with the two methyl groups on the same side of the C=C.
Rotation about the C=C is restricted by the π bond, so the forms are stereoisomers.

questions.subtopic: Skeletal formula for a substituted ring
questions.prompt: Without a supplied diagram, draw the skeletal structure of 1-ethyl-2-methylcyclopropane on paper. Show the two side chains clearly, state the total number of carbon atoms, and explain which atoms and hydrogens are omitted by skeletal notation.
markPoints: The parent cyclopropane is shown as a three-carbon triangular ring.
A two-carbon ethyl substituent is attached to ring carbon 1.
A one-carbon methyl substituent is attached to adjacent ring carbon 2.
The complete structure contains six carbon atoms in total.
Unlabelled line ends/vertices represent carbon, with enough implied hydrogens for normal carbon valency.

questions.prompt: Using only the molecular formula C₄H₈, give or draw one example each of chain and position isomerism among acyclic alkenes. Explain the structural difference in each pair, and say why the examples are isomers rather than different molecular formulae.
markPoints: But-1-ene, CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃, is a valid straight-chain example.
2-Methylpropene, CH₂=C(CH₃)₂, is its chain isomer.
Their carbon skeletons differ although their molecular formulae match.
But-2-ene, CH₃CH=CHCH₃, is a valid position isomer of but-1-ene.
The C=C occupies a different position in the same four-carbon skeleton.
Every proposed structure has molecular formula C₄H₈; a different formula would not be an isomer.

questions.subtopic: Balance a cracking equation and justify cracking
questions.prompt: A hypothetical cracking equation is C₁₂H₂₆ → C₈H₁₈ + X. Determine X, write the balanced equation and explain the commercial reason for cracking long-chain hydrocarbons. Compare the general product emphasis of thermal and catalytic cracking.
markPoints: Carbon conservation gives four carbon atoms in product X.
Hydrogen conservation gives eight hydrogen atoms in product X.
X is C₄H₈, so C₁₂H₂₆ → C₈H₁₈ + C₄H₈ is balanced.
Cracking converts lower-demand heavier fractions into useful fuels and feedstocks.
Thermal cracking tends to give a high proportion of alkenes; catalytic cracking mainly supports motor fuels and aromatic hydrocarbons.

questions.prompt: A hypothetical vehicle exhaust is reported to contain carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides and soot. Explain how the first two pollutants are formed and the main changes a catalytic converter causes to them. Explain why the presence of a catalytic converter does not itself prove that soot has been removed.
markPoints: Carbon monoxide can form when hydrocarbon fuel undergoes incomplete combustion.
At high engine temperatures nitrogen and oxygen from air can react, producing nitrogen oxides.
A catalytic converter oxidises carbon monoxide into carbon dioxide.
A catalytic converter reduces nitrogen oxides to nitrogen.
Solid carbon particles (soot) require different particulate-control measures; a catalytic converter alone is not proof of particle removal.

questions.prompt: Scientists compare upper-atmosphere ozone observations with evidence of chlorine-containing compounds, but correlation alone does not prove a cause. Explain why the ozone layer matters, show with two balanced radical equations how chlorine can catalyse its breakdown, and explain what makes the evidence for restricting CFCs stronger.
markPoints: Upper-atmosphere ozone absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation.
UV radiation can break a C–Cl bond in a CFC, forming a chlorine radical.
Cl• + O₃ → ClO• + O₂ is one propagation step.
ClO• + O₃ → Cl• + 2O₂ is a second balanced step.
The chlorine radical is regenerated, demonstrating a catalytic chain for converting ozone to oxygen.
Independent research, mechanistic evidence and measurements support policy more strongly than a simple correlation by itself.

questions.subtopic: Polyalkene intermolecular forces and PVC uses
questions.prompt: Poly(ethene) and PVC are both addition polymers. Explain why unfunctionalised poly(ethene) chains attract one another and how stronger attractions can arise between longer chains. Then contrast a typical rigid PVC use with a flexible PVC use and the effect of plasticiser molecules.
markPoints: Unfunctionalised poly(ethene) molecules attract primarily through London dispersion forces.
More electrons and greater contact area in longer chains generally strengthen their dispersion attractions.
Unplasticised rigid PVC can be used in drainage pipes or window frames.
Plasticised flexible PVC can be used as electrical cable insulation.
Plasticiser molecules increase chain mobility by weakening how effectively PVC chains attract or pack together.

questions.subtopic: Recover monomer from polymer repeat unit
questions.prompt: A section of an addition polymer is written as [–CH₂–C(CH₃)₂–]ₙ. Draw its alkene monomer on paper and name it. Explain which bond is restored to recover the monomer and why this is addition rather than condensation polymerisation.
markPoints: The monomer has the double bond CH₂=C.
The other double-bond carbon bears two CH₃ groups: CH₂=C(CH₃)₂.
The systematic monomer name is 2-methylpropene.
The repeat-unit backbone single bond between its two carbon atoms is restored to a C=C bond.
The monomers join without elimination of a small molecule, characteristic of addition polymerisation.

questions.subtopic: IR data: suggest a molecular structure
questions.prompt: An unknown molecule has formula C₃H₆O₂. Its IR spectrum shows a strong carbonyl absorption near 1740 cm⁻¹ but lacks the very broad carboxylic-acid O–H absorption. Suggest a plausible named structure with condensed formula, explain the key deductions, and explain what extra IR evidence would help check identity.
markPoints: The absorption near 1740 cm⁻¹ indicates a carbonyl C=O bond.
The missing very broad 2500–3300 cm⁻¹ O–H band argues against an ordinary carboxylic acid.
An ester functional group is a plausible match.
Methyl ethanoate, CH₃COOCH₃, is one valid proposed structure (or another valid C₃H₆O₂ ester).
The proposed structure has exactly three carbon, six hydrogen and two oxygen atoms.
IR alone need not identify a unique isomer; matching the fingerprint region to a reference or other evidence would improve confidence.

questions.prompt: The Earth's surface emits infrared radiation. Explain in molecular terms how carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour influence the outgoing energy budget, and distinguish this process from the role of stratospheric ozone.
markPoints: Carbon dioxide is an atmospheric gas whose molecular vibrations can absorb infrared radiation.
Methane can also absorb infrared radiation at characteristic vibrational frequencies.
Water vapour also absorbs infrared radiation and contributes to the greenhouse effect.
Absorbed radiation can be re-emitted in multiple directions, reducing net outward energy transfer at a given temperature.
Stratospheric ozone's protective role concerns absorption of ultraviolet radiation, not the same mechanism as the greenhouse explanation.

questions.prompt: A hypothetical biofuel lifecycle report states that the growing crop absorbed 1.5 kg of CO₂, use of the fuel released 1.5 kg of CO₂, and associated transport and fertiliser production caused another 0.4 kg of CO₂ emissions. Calculate the net release from the stated data and assess why calling the fuel entirely carbon-neutral could be misleading, including an ethical trade-off.
markPoints: The crop uptake and fuel-use release cancel: 1.5 − 1.5 = 0 kg CO₂ for that part of the cycle.
The stated additional processes contribute 0.4 kg of CO₂ emissions.
Net release for the modelled lifecycle is therefore +0.4 kg CO₂.
This is not entirely carbon-neutral when associated lifecycle emissions are included.
Land and water used to grow fuel crops may compete with food production or ecosystems.
The conclusion depends on lifecycle boundaries and measurement assumptions, so the given estimate is not universal.
